Updated assessment with SLOOS incorporated:
- Policy stance: The FOMC held rates at 5.25–5.50% and tapered QT (lower Treasury runoff caps) due to stalled disinflation and market functioning concerns.
- Financial stability backdrop (FSR): Elevated rate volatility/term premium sensitivity, vulnerabilities in MMFs and leveraged hedge fund basis trades, ongoing CRE stress (especially offices), and public debt/geopolitical tail risks warrant caution.
- SLOOS insight: Banks report tighter lending standards and terms across C&I and consumer credit, wider spreads, higher credit score requirements, and weaker loan demand. CRE underwriting remains notably tighter—lower LTVs, higher DSCRs, shorter interest-only periods, smaller loan sizes, and narrower market coverage—with banks citing economic outlook, risk tolerance, sector-specific issues, and vacancy/rent pressures.
- Policy implications: Tight bank credit supply and weaker loan demand reinforce restrictive financial conditions and should weigh on growth and inflation ahead, reducing the odds of further hikes and supporting patience on cuts until confidence in disinflation improves. QT tapering is consistent with avoiding undue strain in Treasury market functioning amid these vulnerabilities.
- Net tone: Moves from mildly hawkish/near-neutral to slightly cautious/dovish given credit headwinds flagged by SLOOS despite solid activity and strong employment.
